title: A Bruhat order for Latin squares and alternating sign hypermatrices
summary: The Bruhat order on permutation matrices extends to alternating sign matrices via corner-sum matrices, where the order is given by entrywise domination. A classical result of Lascoux and Schützenberger states that alternating sign matrices form the Dedekind-MacNeille completion of the Bruhat order on permutations. Brualdi and Dahl introduced alternating sign hypermatrices as a three-dimensional analogue of alternating sign matrices and used them to generalise Latin squares, which may be viewed as three-dimensional analogues of permutation matrices.
